title: Primary Function
student: Describe the role of the longitudinal rail in supporting the suspended books.
instructor: The rail receives vertical forces from the book hangers, spans between the two interior frame supports, and transfers loading into the frame and floor.

title: External Loads
student: Identify the gravity loads acting on the rail and explain how the books transfer force to it.
instructor: The rail carries uniform self-weight and three groups of downward book weight transmitted by hangers over assigned intervals.

title: Supports and Boundary Conditions
student: Identify the restraints at the two interior supports and the boundary condition at each overhanging end.
instructor: The ideal supports prevent vertical translation but impose no moment; both beam ends are free overhangs.

title: Load Path
student: Trace a book load through the rail, frame, and floor.
instructor: Book weight passes through its hanger to the rail, through support reactions to the frame legs and feet, and into the floor.

title: Critical Locations
student: Before calculating, predict where positive moment, negative support moment, and maximum displacement may occur.
instructor: Negative moments are expected at the interior supports; positive moment and greatest downward displacement are expected between supports, with exact locations set by the unequal loads.

title: Strength and Serviceability
student: Explain why bending stress and vertical deflection require separate checks.
instructor: Stress addresses the assigned flexural-strength limit, while deflection addresses stiffness and usability; either may govern independently.

title: Influential Inputs
student: Explain how span, overhang, section thickness, width, modulus, and load locations influence response.
instructor: Geometry and load locations set reactions and moments; B and especially h control section properties; E and I control elastic deflection.

title: Structural Idealization
student: Draw a 1.50 m overhanging beam with supports, the three occupied intervals, and rail self-weight. Derive one equivalent uniform load for each group; do not draw fifteen separate loads.
instructor: Use supports at x=0.25 and 1.25 m, self-weight over 0–1.50 m, and group UDLs over 0.10–0.25, 0.50–0.70, and 1.20–1.35 m.

title: Modeling Assumptions
student: State the assumptions needed for this one-dimensional linear-elastic beam model.
instructor: Use uniformly transmitted group loads, a prismatic Euler–Bernoulli beam, small deflection, linear elasticity, simple vertical supports, and included self-weight. Exclude local hangers, joints, torsion, uplift details, frame stability, and creep.

title: Analysis Plan
student: Outline a calculation sequence from equivalent loads through the engineering recommendation.
instructor: Calculate four UDLs, solve reactions, form V and M, locate extrema, compute I and S, check stress, integrate curvature with two support conditions, locate deflection extrema, and assess both criteria.

title: Equivalent Loading
student: Calculate rail self-weight and the three equivalent group-load intensities. Explain why fifteen separate load calculations are unnecessary.
instructor: wself={{book_rack_w_self_N_m}} N/m; wA={{book_rack_w_A_N_m}} N/m; wB={{book_rack_w_B_N_m}} N/m; wC={{book_rack_w_C_N_m}} N/m. One statically equivalent UDL represents each uniform group.

title: Support Reactions
student: Draw the complete FBD and calculate Ay and By. Verify force and moment equilibrium.
instructor: Total downward force={{book_rack_W_total_N}} N; Ay={{book_rack_RA_N}} N; By={{book_rack_RB_N}} N. Positive reported values act upward.

title: Shear Diagram
student: Write V(x) in bracket notation and draw the SFD, marking support jumps and loaded intervals.

title: Moment Diagram
student: Integrate shear to obtain M(x), plot the BMD, and identify positive, negative, and governing absolute extrema.
instructor: Mmax,+={{book_rack_M_positive_Nm}} N·m at x={{book_rack_x_M_positive_m}} m. M(a)={{book_rack_M_A_Nm}} N·m; M(b)={{book_rack_M_B_Nm}} N·m. Governing |M|={{book_rack_M_abs_Nm}} N·m.

title: Bending Strength
student: Calculate I and S, then calculate maximum extreme-fiber bending stress and compare it with the assigned allowable.

title: Guided Deflection
student: Use the supplied integrated-curvature expression and v(a)=v(b)=0 to find the greatest absolute vertical deflection. Numerical root finding or a spreadsheet is permitted.
instructor: Maximum downward={{book_rack_v_down_mm}} mm at x={{book_rack_x_v_down_m}} m. Left end={{book_rack_v_left_mm}} mm upward; right end={{book_rack_v_right_mm}} mm upward. Limit={{book_rack_v_allow_mm}} mm; {{book_rack_deflection_check}}.

title: Engineering Assessment
student: Check both criteria. Explain whether passing them proves the complete rack safe and identify one omitted behavior.
